chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman al-Na'ib, from Abdullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Three breaths while drinking is better than one breath while drinking. He also said that it is disliked that it resembles thirsty cattle. I said: And what are thirsty camels? He said: Riding animals. And in another narration it is camels.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method for drinking water according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) recommendation to drink in three breaths, a practice rooted in the Sunnah to aid digestion and prevent overconsumption, while distinguishing the disliked 'hym' (drinking like thirsty camels) from the recommended method. This hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on bodily health as an act of worship, linking physical etiquette to spiritual discipline. The term 'hym' is clarified through scholarly interpretation as either the sound of drinking or the behavior of camels, emphasizing moderation over haste.

en.basel-kadem: 3. Three breaths while drinking is better than one breath while drinking. He also said that it is disliked that it resembles thirsty cattle. I said: And what are thirsty camels? He said: Riding animals. And in another narration it is camels.
